app.title: Codebook reconciler for two coders
app.summary: Two coders have each given every excerpt one code from a shared codebook; the interface shows how far they agree overall and per code, with Cohen's kappa and its strength band. The person works through a queue of the excerpts where the coders differ, optionally narrowed to one code by clicking it in the agreement table, and for each one reads the excerpt beside both coders' codes and definitions, picks A's code, B's code or another, and writes why. When a disagreement shows a definition is unclear, they rewrite it in place and the change is logged with the excerpt that prompted it. They export the final code for every excerpt as CSV and the revised codebook with agreement statistics and the change log as JSON.

task.text: Settle every excerpt two coders coded differently, revising codebook definitions along the way, and export the final codes and the reconciled codebook.

data.text: A codebook of named codes with definitions, and a set of text excerpts from interviews, each given one code by each of two coders; plus the person's resolutions, notes and definition edits.
data.item: an interview excerpt with the code each of two coders gave it

stage.text: reconciling two coders' independent codes and checking their agreement, after coding and before analysis

mechanism.text: A summary bar and a per-code agreement table sit over a queue of disagreements; clicking a code in the table filters the queue, and the selected disagreement opens beside it with the two coders' codes side by side, resolved by click or key, with the definitions in question editable underneath and a log of codebook changes.

field.text: inter-rater reliability of qualitative interview coding against a codebook, in the social sciences

workflow.name: settle disagreements between two coders' labels and revise the scheme

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: overall percent agreement and Cohen's kappa across all codes, plus per-code kappa from a present/absent 2x2 table, each labelled with a Landis and Koch band; codes under 0.6 are bolded

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: clicking a code's row in the agreement table narrows the disagreement queue to excerpts where either coder used that code, with a resolved count and a Show all button

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: a queue of only the excerpts the coders coded differently, each marked Open or Resolved; j and k or Previous and Next move through it, and resolving jumps to the next open one

steps.step: find where people disagree and resolve it
steps.here: the excerpt is shown above coder A's and coder B's codes with their definitions side by side; 1 or 2 takes one coder's code, a dropdown offers any other code, a note field records why for the memo, and Reopen undoes a resolution
the definitions of the two codes in question are editable textareas; saving one logs the old and new wording and the excerpt being discussed, and shows the original under the edited text

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: a bar in the summary shows how many of the disagreements are resolved

a CSV of every excerpt with both coders' codes, whether they agreed, the final code and the resolution note; and a JSON of agreement statistics, the codebook with original and edited definitions, and the change log

distinctive: agreement is measured as Cohen's kappa both overall and per code, banded by Landis and Koch, so the person sees which codes are least reliable before reconciling
each resolution carries a written reason intended for a methods memo, exported alongside the final code
the codebook can be rewritten during reconciliation, and every definition change is logged with the excerpt that prompted it
only the disagreements enter the queue; agreed excerpts pass straight to the final codes
the CSV export warns when disagreements are still open and leaves their final code blank
